chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Idris ibn al-Hassan, from Ali ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Do not testify with a testimony until you recognise it just as you recognise your palm.'

key_terms.تعرف: To know/recognise; implies certainty and direct personal knowledge, not mere supposition
key_terms.شهادة: Testimony, bearing witness; in Islamic jurisprudence refers to both the act of giving evidence in court and the formal legal witness
key_terms.كف: Palm of the hand; chosen as a metaphor for the most immediate and self-evident knowledge

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the conditions for giving testimony in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issued a firm prohibition against bearing witness unless the person has certain and clear knowledge of what they are testifying to — likened to the immediate certainty one has in recognising one's own hand. This teaching reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on absolute certainty (yaqin) as the foundation of valid testimony, protecting both the rights of the accused and the integrity of the judicial process.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Hassan, from Idrees Bin Al Hassan, from Ali Bin Giyas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Do not testify with a testimony until you recognise it just as you recognise your palm’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Idris ibn al-Hassan from Ali ibn Ghiyath who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Do not testify for a case unless you know it as you know your palm.’”
